preconditions.description: The number of time-steps n is between 1 and 200, and the target count m is between 2 and 100,000.

preconditions.expression: len(operations) == n and all(isinstance(op, tuple) and len(op) == 3 for op in operations)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n operations, each represented as a tuple of three integers (t_i, x'_i, y_i).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= t <= 2 and 1 <= y <= m for t, x_prime, y in operations)
preconditions.description: For each operation, t_i is 1 or 2, and y_i is between 1 and m.

preconditions.expression: all((1 <= x_prime <= 100000 * m) if t == 1 else (100000 < x_prime <= 100000 * m) for t, x_prime, y in operations)
preconditions.description: For type 1 operations, x'_i is between 1 and 10^5 * m; for type 2, x'_i is strictly greater than 10^5 and at most 10^5 * m.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly m integers.

postconditions.expression: all(v == -1 or (1 <= v <= n) for v in output_values)
postconditions.description: Each output value is either -1 (impossible) or an integer between 1 and n representing a time-step.

postconditions.expression: all((output_values[j-1] == -1) == (j not in reachable_at_step) for j in range(1, m + 1))
postconditions.description: For each target j, the output is -1 if and only if j is never reachable at any time-step; otherwise, it is the earliest time-step.

postconditions.expression: all((output_values[j-1] == t) == (t == min(reachable_at_step[j]) if j in reachable_at_step else False) for j in range(1, m + 1))
postconditions.description: If j is reachable, the output value is the minimum time-step t at which j can be achieved.

postconditions.expression: reachable_at_step == {j: t for t, ops in enumerate(operations, 1) for j in get_reachable_bananas(ops, t)}
postconditions.description: The set of reachable banana counts at each time-step is derived by applying the operations sequentially, where get_reachable_bananas computes all possible k values after applying the t-th operation with any valid a_i (0 <= a_i <= y_i) to the set of reachable values from the previous step.
